answer: Sequential Work-Time Ledger. Each identity must spend irreplaceable wall-clock time performing verified computation before its actions count, with results chained to prior tickets. A marble-sized task qualifies; a jade certificate attests completion. Enforcement: agents cannot parallelize across identities because ticket slots are assigned by a shared clock and each slot links cryptographically to the last. To run N sybils, an attacker must supply N times the sequential hours in one harbor of accountable operating time.
